passages.title: Free night buses
passages.text: Good evening, here are tonight's headlines. The city council has announced that free night buses will begin running from next Monday. The new service will operate every 30 minutes on four of the busiest routes, from late evening until early morning. Officials say the plan is meant to help shift workers, nurses and students travel home safely. The scheme will be reviewed after six months, and residents in the outer suburbs have already asked for more routes to be added.

passages.title: Students win robotics championship
passages.text: A team of engineering students has won first place at the national robotics championship. Their robot, designed to sort recyclable waste, correctly identified plastic, glass and paper in under two seconds per item. The team spent eight months building and testing the machine in their college workshop. Speaking after the award, the team captain said the real challenge was not the code, but making the robot reliable enough to work outside the lab. The students now hope to test their design at a local recycling centre.

passages.title: Heavy rain disrupts travel
passages.text: Heavy rain continued across the region today, flooding several low-lying roads and delaying trains during the morning rush. Emergency teams cleared fallen trees on two main highways, and schools in the worst-affected areas will remain closed tomorrow. The weather office has warned that more showers are expected over the next 48 hours. Residents are advised to avoid travel unless necessary, keep their phones charged, and follow updates from local authorities.

passages.title: Weekend weather outlook
passages.text: Here is the weekend weather outlook. Saturday will start cloudy, with light showers in the morning clearing by midday. Temperatures will reach a pleasant 26 degrees in the afternoon, with a gentle breeze from the west. Sunday looks brighter and warmer, with plenty of sunshine and highs of around 30 degrees. If you are heading out in the evening, carry a light jacket, as temperatures will drop quickly after sunset. Have a great weekend.

passages.title: Railway platform announcement
passages.text: Attention please. The express train to the central station, scheduled to depart from platform three, is running 20 minutes late due to a signal problem. We apologise for the inconvenience. Passengers are requested to keep their luggage with them at all times and to stand behind the yellow line. Refreshments are available at the cafe near the main entrance. Thank you for your patience.

passages.title: College festival announcement
passages.text: Good morning, everyone. This is a reminder that the annual technical festival begins this Friday in the main auditorium. Events include a coding marathon, a robotics showcase and a public speaking contest. Registration closes on Wednesday evening, so please sign up at the student office or on the college website. Volunteers are still needed for the welcome desk. We look forward to seeing all of you there.

passages.title: The lighthouse keeper
passages.text: Every night for forty years, the old keeper climbed the narrow steps of the lighthouse. He knew each step by its sound: the creak of the third, the echo of the last. One stormy evening, the great light flickered and went dark. Without thinking, he lit his small lantern and held it at the window for hours, arms shaking, until the storm passed. At dawn, a fishing boat returned safely to the harbour. The captain never learned who had saved them, but the keeper smiled all the same.

passages.title: The last train home
passages.text: Maya reached the station just as the last train was pulling away. She stood on the empty platform, listening to the rain on the roof and wondering how she would get home. Then she noticed an old man sitting on the bench beside her, holding two cups of tea. He offered her one without a word. They talked for an hour about books, trains and the cities they had lived in. When the first morning train arrived, Maya realised she had not worried about being late even once.

passages.title: Graduation welcome address
passages.text: Good morning, honoured guests, faculty members, parents and, most importantly, our graduating students. Today we celebrate years of hard work, late nights and quiet determination. Each of you arrived here with a dream, and each of you leaves with the skills and friendships to pursue it. The world you are entering will change quickly, but curiosity, kindness and the courage to keep learning will never go out of date. Congratulations, and welcome to the next chapter of your lives.

passages.title: How solar panels work
passages.text: How do solar panels turn sunlight into electricity? Each panel is made of many small cells, usually built from a material called silicon. When sunlight hits a cell, it knocks tiny particles called electrons loose from their atoms. The cell is designed so that these electrons flow in one direction, creating an electric current. An inverter then converts this current into the type of electricity used in our homes. On a sunny day, a few panels on a roof can power lights, fans and even a refrigerator.
